name: SwaposV2Pair constant-product check 100 times too lenient
summary: SwaposV2Pair.swap scales the post-swap balances by 10000 (balance*10000 - amountIn*10) but compares their product with reserve0*reserve1*1000**2, so a swap passes as long as the new product is at least 1% of the old one and any caller can take almost the whole pool for dust. Every pair of the Swapos factory 0x78520513, deployed hours earlier, carried it. The anchor is the MEV bot 0xc0ffeebabe's arbitrage loop, which cycled USDC into the USDC/SWP pair 0x3f2892a1, the SWP into the SWP/WETH pair 0xdbc74ed1 and the WETH back through Uniswap V3 seven times at unchanged pair prices, taking 4.85 WETH for 8,231 USDC; other bots repeated such loops, and three hours later 0x53fc4a4a sent 10 wei to the SWP/WETH pair 0x8ce2f928 and the WETH/USDC and USDC/WBTC pairs and swapped out 155.37 WETH, 95,271.59 USDC, 1.56 WBTC and 143,211 SWP.
notes: Anchor: Sync events of all ten pairs the factory created (blocks 17055825-17056652) were checked for swaps that lowered reserve0*reserve1, which the Uniswap V2 check forbids. The first is 0x06dc6e91 (block 17056426, index 0) by 0xc0ffeebabe5d, a general MEV bot unrelated to Swapos, whose seven identical cycles each lowered both pairs' products by 2-35%; 20 bot transactions followed before the DeFiHackLabs attacker's 0xbe643ccd (block 17057420), which drained 0x8ce2f928, a pair created at block 17056652 after the anchor. 35 product-lowering swaps in all, to block 23000000. campaign.mjs over both targets and the eight siblings to block 17060000 finds only ordinary router swaps before the anchor.

Targets are the two pairs the anchor swapped through, each aged from its creation by the factory; the other eight pairs are sibling deployments in the campaign (rule 4). The factory 0x78520513 was deployed at block 17055714 and the pairs carry no upgradeable code.

Loss is the Swapos pairs' gross depletion per asset over the anchor and the campaign (loss.mjs, the ten factory pairs as victims, DefiLlama prices at each transaction; MATIC at 1.1 USD). The USDC and ETH the bots paid into the pairs in their swaps (10,285.26 USDC, 0.20 ETH) are not subtracted (rule 11); netting them in each transaction instead gives 477,574 USD, of which 469,080 came from 0x53fc4a4a's three drains. Both SWP tokens (0x09176f68, 0xb4a4080d) have no market and the attackers did not sell them, so they count at zero (rule 12); DefiLlama lists the incident at 468k USD.
